newsitem.title: RUSSIA: U.S. astronaut may substitute Russian in repairs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. astronaut may substitute Russian in repairs.

text.p: A NASA official said on Tuesday Russian mission controllers had asked that a U.S. astronaut on board the crippled Mir space station be prepared to do vital repairs in place of ailing cosmonaut Vasily Tsibliyev.

"If it is necessary we can do this," Philip Engelauf told reporters, adding that British-born Michael Foale had been fully trained for the mission. Tsibliyev complained of cardiovascular problems on Monday. The repair works, scheduled for Friday or Saturday, have been postponed.

During a radio link-up, Russian ground staff were heard by journalists telling Tsibliyev to do what he could to pass his experience of space walks to Foale, but also to tell the American he should not feel under pressure to accept the job.
The repair work is intended to restore power lost after Mir's collision with a cargo craft on June 25, the worst accident in the station's 11 years in space.
There was no further information on Tsibliyev's health. A special committee of doctors was to meet during the day to discuss the problem.
A NASA representative told Reuters earlier at Russian Mission Control near Moscow that the postponement of repair works might also delay the launch of a spacecraft with a relief crew.
